title: Carry the bee binary into a freshly bootstrapped worktree store
action:
Reproduced live on 2026-08-21: `bee worktree new --feature <slug>` created and granted the worktree, copied `onboarding.json` and `config.json`, and synced skills — but `.bee/bin/` in the new worktree held no `bee` binary at all, so every `.bee/bin/bee ...` call from inside it died with `No such file or directory`. AGENTS.md tells agents to run bee as `.bee/bin/bee`, and the worktree is where feature work is supposed to happen, so a fresh worktree is unusable until someone copies the binary by hand. The binary is gitignored, so `git worktree add` cannot carry it and the bootstrap does not either.

Fix in `bootstrap_worktree_store` (packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/worktree/registry.rs:811-916), beside the existing `copy_if_absent("onboarding.json")` / `copy_if_absent("config.json")` pair at :838-839.

Shape — LINK FIRST, COPY AS FALLBACK. Add a sibling helper (do NOT widen `copy_if_absent`, which is file-in-store-root shaped and returns a different report) that provisions `<worktree>/.bee/bin/bee` from `<main_store_root>/bin/bee`:
1. Source resolution: prefer `bin/bee`, and on Windows `bin/bee.exe` — probe both and take whichever exists, exactly the way the repo's own hook shim probes the pair. Absent source: report `{provisioned:false, reason:"main store has no bin/bee"}` and DO NOT fail the bootstrap — a host that never installed a binary must still get its worktree.
2. Destination already exists: report `{provisioned:false, reason:"bin/bee already exists"}` and leave it alone, matching `copy_if_absent`'s idempotence. `bootstrap_worktree_store` re-runs on `worktree register` against an already-adopted worktree, so this MUST be idempotent.
3. Create `<worktree>/.bee/bin/` when absent.
4. Try a symlink first: `std::os::unix::fs::symlink` under `#[cfg(unix)]`, `std::os::windows::fs::symlink_file` under `#[cfg(windows)]`. A symlink cannot go stale — a rebuilt main binary is instantly live in every worktree, which a copy cannot promise and which `bee doctor`'s binary_freshness row would otherwise start reporting per worktree.
5. If the symlink call fails for ANY reason — Windows without Developer Mode or admin privileges is the real case, but treat every error the same — fall back to `std::fs::copy` and, on unix, restore the source's executable permission bit on the destination (a plain `fs::copy` preserves mode on unix, but assert it rather than assume: read the source metadata's mode and set it). A copy that also fails reports `{provisioned:false, reason:<the io error>}` and still does not fail the bootstrap.
6. Report which happened: add one `"binary"` key to the returned map on BOTH return paths — the early `state.json already exists` return at :908-913 and the fresh-state return at :909-915 — carrying `{provisioned:bool, method:"symlink"|"copy"|null, reason?:string}`. Both paths already carry `onboarding`, `config` and `identity`; the new key rides beside them so `worktree new`'s and `worktree register`'s own output shows it.

Tests in the module's existing test style, using a temp directory (see the fixture at prune.rs:852 for how a main store is seeded):
(a) a main store holding `bin/bee` bootstraps a worktree whose `.bee/bin/bee` exists and resolves to the same content;
(b) the report's `binary.provisioned` is true and `method` is one of symlink|copy;
(c) a second bootstrap over the same worktree leaves the existing entry untouched and reports `provisioned:false` with the already-exists reason — the idempotence `worktree register` depends on;
(d) a main store with NO `bin/bee` still bootstraps green, with `binary.provisioned:false` and a named reason — the bootstrap must never fail on a missing binary;
(e) on unix, when the fallback copy path is taken, the destination is executable. Drive the fallback directly through the helper rather than by breaking symlink support, if that is what the code shape allows; if it is not reachable without contorting the code, say so in the deviation rather than inventing a seam.

truths: A worktree created by bee worktree new can run .bee/bin/bee with no hand-copying
A main store with no bin/bee still bootstraps a worktree green
A second bootstrap over the same worktree never replaces an existing .bee/bin/bee

key_links: bootstrap_worktree_store reports the binary provisioning beside onboarding/config/identity on both return paths
prohibitions: No change to copy_if_absent's own shape or its two existing callers
No change to the fresh state.json contents or to the cells sync
The bootstrap must never fail because the binary could not be provisioned

report.outcome: bootstrap_worktree_store provisions <worktree>/.bee/bin/bee from the main store (symlink first, mode-preserving copy fallback), reports it under a new binary key on both return paths, and refuses idempotently on any existing destination including a dangling link.
report.tests: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml worktree — green (221 passed, 0 failed) — the cell changes one product file plus one assertion in the worktree test module; the independent judge additionally reproduced the safety fence out of tree by reverting the guard and observing the clobber
deviations: Stacked a second commit (98675cb6) instead of amending 983bbd91: the sibling worker on srg-1 committed eb769d70 on top while srg-2 was being revised, so amending would have rewritten a live sibling commit hash inside a shared worktree. Both commits carry the srg-2 trailer.

Tests live in a new #[cfg(test)] mod inside registry.rs rather than worktree/tests.rs, which a sibling reservation held; one line of worktree/tests.rs still had to move because the new binary key is mandated on the fresh return path.

Hardened beyond the brief: the destination check uses fs::symlink_metadata, not exists(). exists() follows symlinks, so a stale-target link would read as absent and the fallback fs::copy would write THROUGH it into main s own bin/, destroying the real binary from a worktree bootstrap. The judge reproduced that clobber.
Test (e) drives copy_worktree_binary directly rather than through a faked symlink refusal — unix never takes the fallback and the helper is already a clean seam.
